info.title: MXroute Email Hosting API
info.description:
REST API for managing MXroute email hosting accounts.

## Authentication

All API requests require three HTTP headers:

| Header | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `X-Server` | Your mail server hostname (e.g., `eagle.mxlogin.com`) |
| `X-Username` | Your DirectAdmin username, or `reseller\|user` for an owned user |
| `X-API-Key` | Your complete API key password, or account password if permitted by DirectAdmin |

Create API keys in your [mxpanel dashboard](https://panel.mxroute.com/api-keys.php).
Send the complete credential unchanged, including any colons. Do not prepend
the key ID; legacy `keyid:password` parsing is no longer supported.
Account passwords require DirectAdmin to permit password-based API access
(`api_with_password=yes` in the account's `user.conf`). Login keys are
unaffected by that setting.

### Reseller impersonation

To manage an owned user, send `X-Username: reseller|user` with the reseller's
own complete API key in `X-API-Key` and their server in `X-Server`.
Each name must contain 1–16 letters, digits or underscores. Chained pipes
and self-impersonation are rejected; use a plain username for your own account.

The API verifies the credential owner's reseller role, then authenticates
to DirectAdmin as `reseller|user`. DirectAdmin must authorize the target;
the returned real and effective identities must match. Only ordinary user
targets are supported. Admin credentials and user-to-user impersonation
are not supported by this feature. The key's DirectAdmin restrictions remain
in force and must permit session queries, impersonation and the requested action.

All account and domain operations apply to the target user. Reseller-only
endpoints are unavailable while impersonating; send the plain reseller
username to manage users or packages. The reseller and all impersonated
targets share the reseller's rate-limit bucket on that server.

```bash
curl 'https://api.mxroute.com/domains' \
  -H 'X-Server: eagle.mxlogin.com' \
  -H 'X-Username: reseller|user' \
  -H 'X-API-Key: YOUR_RESELLER_API_KEY'
```

## Rate Limits

| Operation Type | Limit |
|----------------|-------|
| Read (GET) | 200 requests/minute |
| Write (POST, PATCH, DELETE) | 60 requests/minute |
| Bulk/import | 10 requests/minute |

Rate limit headers are included in every response:
- `X-RateLimit-Limit`: Maximum requests allowed
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: Requests remaining in window
- `X-RateLimit-Reset`: Unix timestamp when limit resets

## Error Responses

All errors follow this format:
```json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "ERROR_CODE",
    "message": "Human-readable message",
    "field": "field_name"  // Optional, for validation errors
  }
}
```

Common error codes:
- `VALIDATION_ERROR` - Invalid input data
- `UNAUTHORIZED` - Invalid or missing credentials
- `FORBIDDEN` - Insufficient permissions
- `NOT_FOUND` - Resource not found
- `CONFLICT` - Resource already exists
- `BUSINESS_ERROR` - Business logic violation (e.g., limit reached)
- `RATE_LIMITED` - Too many requests
- `SERVER_ERROR` - Internal server error

tags.name: Spam Settings
tags.description:
Spam filter configuration. Sender lists are shared across an account's domains.
Every operation requires an owned domain. Writes preserve unrelated settings.
Request bodies are limited to 2048 bytes and accept only the documented field.
Unsupported or unavailable upstream settings cause an error, never default values.
Updates to the same account are serialized across the panel and REST API.
After an unconfirmed save, read the settings before deciding whether to retry.

apiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
apiKeyAuth.description:
Your complete API key password (created at panel.mxroute.com/api-keys.php),
or account password if DirectAdmin permits password-based API access.
Sent unchanged, including colons. Do not prepend a key ID.
For reseller impersonation, use the reseller's key, not the target user's.
Example: `[API_KEY_FROM_SECRET_STORE]`

serverAuth.name: X-Server
serverAuth.description:
Your mail server hostname (shown on API Keys page).
Example: `eagle.mxlogin.com`

usernameAuth.name: X-Username
usernameAuth.description:
Your DirectAdmin username (shown on API Keys page), or `reseller|user`
to act as an ordinary user owned by that reseller. Each name is 1–16
letters, digits or underscores. Use the reseller's key with the pipe form.
Examples: `johndoe`, `reseller|johndoe`.

operations.description:
Returns your domain verification key, which must be added as a DNS TXT record
before adding new domains to your account.

**Automation workflow:**
1. Call this endpoint to get your verification key
2. Add a TXT record to your domain: `{key}.yourdomain.com` with value `domain-verified`
3. Wait for DNS propagation (typically 5-15 minutes)
4. Call `POST /domains` to add the domain

name.description: Use this as the record name (prepend to your domain)

data.description: Add this TXT record to your domain before adding it to your account
